regime.label: The 1060 break fails: future reclaims the gamma hinge by 2.3 points and dealer GEX rebuilds 497% to +1,188, but the pin is thin-tethered at 25 DTE
evidence: Net dealer GEX is +1,188 today versus +199 yesterday, a 497% rebuild, yet still only 30% of the +3,914 cushion on 25 Aug and 59% of the +2,019 five sessions ago (29 Aug) - the damping is back but it is a fraction of the size that held the 1065-1075 chop.

Spot 1062.3 sits 2.3 points above the 1060 hinge, exactly reversing yesterday's 1.7-point break below it: per-strike net GEX is +5 at 1060, +722 at 1070, +3,039 at 1080 and +2,392 at 1100 against -2,590 at 1050 and -2,011 at 1030, so hedging caps rallies and amplifies dips from the same 1060 pivot (the cumulative sum only crosses zero at 1110 on thin far-OTM call OI, so 1060 remains the working flip).

Max pain is 1060 for the second session and spot is 2.3 points (0.2%) from it, with the heaviest balanced near-money OI on the board at that strike (1,352 calls versus 1,350 puts) - but 25 DTE and cash settlement mean ATM gamma has not yet steepened enough to tether price.

Put OI hit a window record 42,069 (+357 today, +1,037 over five sessions) while call OI fell 568 to 18,968 and ATM IV collapsed 0.98 points to 13.11%, the lowest since 13.00% on 26 Aug: protection is still accumulating even as its price falls, which is insurance demand rather than a directional bet.

S50U26.today_summary: 1062.3 on the front future, up 4.0 points on the day and back 2.3 points above the 1060 gamma hinge it lost yesterday, sitting effectively on max pain at 1060. Net dealer GEX rebuilt 497% to +1,188 from +199, restoring a long-gamma cap across 1070-1100 (+3,039 at 1080 alone) while leaving a short-gamma trapdoor of -2,590 at 1050 and -2,011 at 1030. ATM IV fell 0.98 points to 13.11% and 25-delta skew halved to +1.05 from +1.98, so downside protection is the cheapest it has been since 26 Aug - even as put OI printed a window record 42,069 and put/call OI rose to 2.22. Total volume was light at 3,854 lots, down 19.7% from 4,797 yesterday, so today's rebuild is as much decay and repricing as fresh conviction.
what_changed: Net GEX rebuilt to +1,188 from +199 yesterday (+497%) as the future reclaimed 1060, but it remains 70% below the +3,914 reading of 25 Aug - the cushion is thinner than the headline rebound implies.

ATM IV compressed 0.98 points to 13.11% and 25-delta skew halved to +1.05 from +1.98 (peak +2.90 on 2 Sep), pricing the failed break as noise and making defined-risk downside structures cheaper than at any point since 26 Aug.

Put OI set a window record 42,069, up 1,037 over five sessions, concentrated at 1020 (+223), 1030 (+190) and 950 (+166) - the build sits squarely inside the short-gamma pocket below 1060, not above it.

Call OI fell 218 at the 1100 wall over five sessions while 1070 gained 151 and 1080 gained 68: overhead resistance is migrating down toward spot and thinning at the top, with 1100 volume down to 184 lots from 404 yesterday.
S50U26.five_day_thesis: Over five sessions the future is down 3.1 points from 1065.4 (29 Aug) while max pain held 1060 and the 1100 call wall and 1050 near-money put wall have not moved once in nine sessions - the structure is anchored, the price is drifting inside it. The live change is the gamma cushion: net GEX ran +2,019 (29 Aug) to +2,762 to +199 to +1,188, never once flipping sign in aggregate but collapsing and rebuilding around the 1060 hinge, which itself migrated 1080 to 1060 and has now been tested from both sides in two sessions. Protection kept accumulating through all of it - put OI +1,037 to a record 42,069 with +413 of that at 1020-1030 - while the price of that protection fell, 25-delta skew easing from +1.56 to +1.05 and ATM IV from 13.44% to 13.11%. That divergence, OI up and vol down, is the tell: this is systematic insurance being layered into the September series, not panic, and Vol2Vol confirms it is live at 1050 (286 lots traded today, OI +34) but decaying at 1100 (volume 184 versus 404, OI -218 over five sessions). With 17 trading sessions left, the 1-sigma cone of 8.78 points per day projects a 1026-1099 range to expiry - which is precisely the 10-delta band the chain already prices at 1020/1100.

strategies.name: Iron condor 1020P / 1000P x 1100C / 1120C
strategies.rationale: Short strikes sit outside both live near-money walls (1050 put, 1100 call) and on the 10-delta band the chain itself prices, expressing the +1,188 long-gamma cap above 1060 with ATM IV at 13.11%; short-vol payoff is negative-skew so this is the small-size expression, not the core.
strategies.defined_risk: Net credit approximately 3.4 points; max loss = 20-point wing width minus credit, approximately 16.6 points on whichever side is breached.
strategies.invalidation: A close below 1050 (into the -2,590 short-gamma pocket) or above 1100 (the call wall) breaks the range assumption.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1050 / 1020
strategies.rationale: 25-delta skew at +1.05 is the cheapest since 26 Aug while put OI is at a record 42,069 and the 1020-1050 band carries -7,600 of net GEX, so a break of 1060 gets amplified rather than absorbed - this buys that trapdoor at the point where insurance is cheapest relative to the demand for it.
strategies.defined_risk: Net debit approximately 6.2 points (1050 put 10.1 minus 1020 put 3.9); max loss = the 6.2-point debit, max value 30 points minus debit.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1080, where the +3,039 long-gamma shelf caps the move and the downside thesis stops paying.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1080 / 1100
strategies.rationale: 1080 is both the 25-delta call strike and the single largest positive gamma shelf (+3,039), so dealers sell into rallies there, and the 1100 wall above it is decaying (OI -218 over five sessions, volume 184 versus 404) - this is the rally-cap expression and an alternative to the condor's call wing, not an addition to it.
strategies.defined_risk: Net credit approximately 4.1 points; max loss = 20-point width minus credit, approximately 15.9 points.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1090 with call OI rebuilding at 1100 - that turns the thinning wall into a squeeze target rather than resistance.

S50U26.prediction: 1053-1071 is the 1-sigma daily cone around 1062.3, and the 1060 hinge plus max pain at 1060 argues for chop inside it while net GEX stays positive. The asymmetry is downward: a close below 1050 hands dealers -2,590 of gamma at that strike and opens the 1020-1030 pocket where +413 put lots were added in five sessions, while the +3,039 shelf at 1080 caps the upside first. The bias is invalidated above 1080 on rebuilding call OI, or below 1050 on expanding volume and rising IV, which would be the short-gamma amplification case rather than a pin.
S50U26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice and not a recommendation to execute any position. SET50 options are European and cash-settled on the SET50 index, so there is no physical delivery and the dealer-hedging mechanics that drive pinning are structurally weaker than for share-settled single stocks: treat the 1060 max-pain anchor as a tendency, not a guarantee, especially at 25 DTE where ATM gamma has not yet steepened. Defined risk is not risk-free - the capped maximum loss on every structure above is real and does occur. Macro or news flow can override the option structure outright; if price leaves the 1050-1080 band on expanding volume and rising IV, that is real flow beating the structure and the mean-reversion read should be dropped, not doubled.
